prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Signing in automatically restores your saved pets and progress from previous sessions."]
1: ["Quick Hotkeys: Press Alt+P to toggle visibility, Alt+H to hide, Alt+C to open chat"]
2: ["Master Desktop Pet Hotkeys", "Try out your pet controls so you can interact with your companion effortlessly.", "Alt+P: Show/Hide Pet | Alt+M: Mute Audio | Alt+C: Chat Box"]
3: ["Preparing high-res desktop animations. Your pet will launch automatically in moments."]
4: ["Analyzing photo features and building pet behaviors... Processing takes around 1-2 minutes."]
5: ["Your pet progress and customizations automatically transfer across all signed-in devices."]
6: ["Practice Controlling Your Pet", "Test your hotkeys now to summon, hide, or chat with your new pet.", "Test Summon (Alt+P)"]
7: []
8: ["We'll notify you as soon as your pet is ready to appear on your desktop."]
9: ["Signing in secures your adoption certificate and preserves pet personality data safe in the cloud."]
